questions.question: Explain the difference between primary memory and secondary memory
questions.solution_html:
• Primary memory (like RAM) is volatile, meaning it loses data when power is off, and is
  • directly accessed by the CPU for active tasks. Secondary memory (like Hard Drives/USBs) is
  • non-volatile, meant for permanent storage, and is slower than primary memory.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: non-volatile, meant for permanent storage, and is slower than primary memory.

questions.question: Describe how headers, footers, and page breaks support navigation and structure in a long document.
questions.solution_html:
• Headers/Footers: These provide consistent context on every page, such as the
  • document title, chapter name, or page numbers. This helps the reader know exactly
  • where they are in the document.
  • Page Breaks: These are used to force content to start on a new page. Instead of
  • pressing "Enter" multiple times, a page break ensures that a new chapter or major
  • section always starts cleanly at the top of a page, maintaining professional formatting.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: section always starts cleanly at the top of a page, maintaining professional formatting.

questions.question: Explain how guides and rulers help in aligning and organizing content in In Design.
questions.solution_html:
• Rulers: Located at the top and side of the workspace, they provide precise
  • measurements (inches, cm, pixels) to place objects accurately.
  • Guides: These are non-printing lines you can pull from the rulers. They act as a visual
  • grid, helping you align text boxes, images, and headlines perfectly with each other.
  • This ensures the layout looks organized and professional rather than messy.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: This ensures the layout looks organized and professional rather than messy.

questions.question: A journalist is preparing a magazine article — describe how text alignment and line spacing affect the visual appeal of the document.
questions.solution_html:
• Alignment: Using "Justified" alignment gives the text clean, straight edges on both
  • sides, which is standard for professional magazines. Left alignment creates a "ragged"
  • edge which is more casual.
  • Line Spacing (Leading): If lines are too close, the text looks dense and intimidating
  • to read. Increasing the line spacing introduces "white space," making the article look
  • lighter, more inviting, and easier for the eye to track.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: lighter, more inviting, and easier for the eye to track.

questions.question: Describe the process of creating and saving a document in MS Word, including different file formats (DOCX, PDF) and folder organization for easy retrieval
questions.solution_html:
• Creating: Launch MS Word and select "Blank Document." Enter your text. Use the
  • ribbon tools to format the font, paragraphs, and styles to create a professional look.
  • Saving: Click the File tab and select Save As.
  • o DOCX: Choose this format if you want to keep the file editable. It is the
  • standard format for Word.
  • o PDF: Choose this format if you are finalizing the document for distribution. It
  • ensures that the formatting (fonts, images) looks exactly the same on every
  • computer and prevents accidental editing.
  • Folder Organization: In the "Save As" dialog, avoid saving everything to the
  • Desktop. Use the "New Folder" button to create a specific folder (e.g., "Semester 1
  • Notes"). Naming files clearly (e.g., "Assignment_1_Draft.docx") and placing them in
  • subject-specific folders ensures you can quickly find them later without searching
  • through a cluttered list.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: through a cluttered list.

questions.question: You are asked to prepare a budget table in Excel. Explain how merging cells and adjusting column width/row height improves clarity and readability.
questions.solution_html:
• Merging Cells for Titles: A budget needs a clear title. By selecting cells A1 to E1
  • and clicking "Merge & Center," the title "Monthly Budget" is centered across the
  • entire table. This creates a strong visual hierarchy, telling the viewer immediately
  • what the sheet is about.
  • Adjusting Column Width: Default columns are often too narrow. If a cell contains
  • "Miscellaneous Expenses," it might get cut off or overlap. Double-clicking the
  • column boundary (AutoFit) expands the column so the full text is visible. This
  • prevents data from being hidden or misread.
  • Adjusting Row Height: The header row (Date, Item, Cost) needs to stand out.
  • Increasing the row height adds "breathing room" (white space) around the text. This
  • separation distinguishes the headers from the data rows below, making the table less
  • cramped and easier to scan for specific information.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: cramped and easier to scan for specific information.
